title: Tulip Mania's Priciest Flowers Were Sick 🌷

scenes.say: The most expensive tulips in history were sick.
In the sixteen thirties, the Dutch paid fortunes for broken tulips, streaked with flames of colour.
Nobody could grow one on purpose. A plain bulb might break into stripes, or not.
And broken bulbs were weak. They made fewer baby bulbs, so supply stayed tiny.
In the nineteen twenties, scientists found the cause: a virus, spread by tiny aphids.
People paid fortunes for a disease. What do we overpay for today, just because it's rare?
